info.title: BPCE Open Finance Transfer
info.description:
Enables partners applications to initiate a transfer without enforcing our common end user customers to use their BPCE internet bank site interface. Also enables to check-in information of a new recipient in the BPCE systems to permit future transfers.

# Authentication

This API is secured with standard Authorization `Oauth2` flows.

## Initial Authorization request
The Authorization request uses `PKCE` method and so it uses a `code_challenge_method` parameter set to "S256" - see [RFC7636](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636).

## Authorization process
In presence of our common end user client, the partner application begins the authorization process by accessing a "BPCE CONNECT" URL. Some parameters of the HTTP request are required and must be compliant to information registered in our systems during the registration of the partner application (`client id`, `redirection uri`, `cancel redirection uri`). The `PKCE` `code_challenge` is also required.
By this initial request call, the "BPCE CONNECT" web page enables the end user to authenticate himself to our system by using his current bank identifiers and authentication methods.
At the end of this process, if the authentication is OK, the "BPCE CONNECT" process uses the redirection uri to give the `Oauth2` authorization code to the partner application.

## Get a token
The partner application must send a GET `Oauth2` token request with `grant_type` parameter set to "authorization_code" and must provide the authorization code.

# Concepts
This API deals with bank transfers initiation and related needed concepts ; the main one is obviously the notion of bank account : customers' internal accounts and recipient accounts, since a bank transfer is a money transfer from a debited account (belonging to the customer who orders the transfer) to a recipient account.

## Common end user customer
In order to access any endpoint of this API, the presence of the common end user customer is required.
A common end user customer is :
 - a person who is a customer of one of the bank establishments of the BPCE banking group (mainly `Caisse d'Epargne` and `Banque Populaire`) who has entered into a contract to have access to the BPCE website,
 - a person who is a customer of the partner.
 
## Subscriber
By subscriber, we mean a user of the bank's website. Via a contract with his remote bank, he has an identifier allowing him to connect to his remote bank. Throughout the remainder of this contract, the methods of this API can only be reached by the subscriber. Indeed, the authentication prior to the consumption of the API is the authentication of the subscriber. Moreover, he uses his remote bank identifier to authenticate himself and obtain access to this API. Physically, the subscriber can be confused with the common end customer.

## Transfer
As indicated above, a bank transfer is a money transfer from a debited account (that belongs to the customer who orders the transfer) to a recipient account.

### Transfer request
In this API, a transfer request is the order by the end user customer to create one or several transfer orders within BPCE systems. A transfer request contains one and only transfer source account that will be debited. A transfer request contains one or several transfer recipient accounts that will be credited.

### Transfer request line
By this terminology, one designates an individual bank transfer within a transfer request. So a transfer request line is the part of the transfer request which will be processed furthermore by a transfer.

### Transfer source account
The source account of a transfer is the account that is debited by the transfer operation.
It must be an internal account (see below).
The common end user customer must have the rights to debit this account : either the account belongs to him, either he has a mandate on it.

### Transfer recipient account
The recipient account of a transfer is the account that is credited by the transfer operation.

### Type of a transfer request line (transfer type)
For the moment, this API deals only with [SCT scheme transfers](https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/what-we-do/sepa-credit-transfer), that is SEPA transfer with an amount in euro.

### Out of scope transfer request line types
For the moment, the following transfer types are out of scope :
- account to account transfer (between two accounts that both belong to the end user customer and are both managed in the same BPCE establishment)
- SEPA Instant Payment
- transfer cash
- internationnal transfer (SWIFT etc.)

## Internal account
An internal account is managed by the end user customer's BPCE bank establishment (in which he has authenticated into).

## External account
An external account may designate an account managed by any bank establishment (that is not necessarly the same bank establishement of the transfer source account). An external account not necessarly belongs to the customer.
For the moment, the external accounts are identified by an [IBAN](https://www.iso.org/fr/standard/81090.html).

# Use cases
The following use cases demonstrate how to use the API.

## Initiating a transfer

In order to be able to create a new transfer request order, one needs to identify a source account and one or several recipient accounts.

1. Firstly, get the internal account list that belongs to the customer with _Get the internal accounts_ (`GET /internalAccounts`). Memorize the identifier of the chosen internal account that will be the transfer source account.
1. Secondly, get the external account list that the customer has check-in in our systems with _Get the external accounts_ (`GET /externalAccounts`). Memorize the identifiers of the chosen external accounts.
1. Create a transfer request with _Create a transfer request_ (`POST /transferRequests`). Once the request is called, some transfer orders will be registered but they will be set in a `TO_VALIDATE` status, and so they they will not be processed as long as the transfer request is not confirmed.
1. Get the transfer request status with _Read transfer request characteristics_ (`GET /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}`). While the status is `INITIALIZED`, the partner application has to redo the same call with temporisation. Once the status is `CONFIRMABLE`, one can go to next step (confirmation).
1. Optionnaly, one can add transfer lines to the transfer request with _Add additional transfers within a transfer request_ (`POST /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}/transferRequestLines`).
1. Confirm a transfer request with a first call to _Confirm a transfer request_ (`POST /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}/confirmations`).
1. In a general way, an error HTTP 403 is returned with a specific header "X-Stepup-Token" to indicate that is necessary for the caller application to enter into a step-up process (within a strong authentication) to seal the transfer request.
1. In presence of a such response, please call "BPCE_CONNECT" to enter into a step-up process.
1. After having do the strong authentification and completing the step-up process, redo a second call to _Confirm a transfer request_ (`POST /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}/confirmations`) with the access token that was just generated in order to do the confirmation action.
1. For some transfer request, none step-up process is required, so the first call to _Confirm a transfer request_ (`POST /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}/confirmations`) will directly succeed.
1. In particular and rare cases, besides the confirmation of the transfer request is necessary, it will be not allowed at all via a call to _Confirm a transfer request_ (`POST /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}/confirmations`) ; in this case, a specific error indicates the end user customer to validate the transfer within the BPCE web site.

### Consistency checks between transfer request line
When creating a transfer request, one checks the coherence of the lines set :
- if requested debit mode is equal to `GROUPED`
  - each line must debit the same internal account,
  - each line must have the same requested date for delayed transfers,
  - each line must have the same deadline type.
- if requested debit mode is equal to `SINGLE`
  - each line contains a single transfer (the internal account, deadline type and the requested date can be different).

## Getting transfer request characteristics
The partner application may offer a way to the end user customer to get information about the done transfer request.

### Getting transfer request global information
1. Get global information of a transfer request with _Read transfer request characteristics_ (`GET /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}`). In response, one can get the transfer request status which describes the current state of the entry phase.

### Getting transfer request lines
1. Get the pagined list of transfer request lines with _Get the transfer request lines list_ (`GET /transferRequestLines`). The identifier of the transfer request may be passed by the transferRequestId parameter. Each returned item contains a transfer request line identifier which enables to get detailed information on it.

### Getting transfer request errors
1. Get the error list that occured during the transfer request check-in with _List of errors in a transfer request_ (`GET /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}/errors`). These errors are furnished in order to inform the end user customer and may forbid the transfer request confirmation.

### Getting details of a transfer request line
1. Get the pagined list of transfer request lines with _Get the transfer request lines list_ (`GET /transferRequestLines`) in order to get the line identifier of the searched transfer request line.
1. Get the details of transfer request line with _Get a Transfer Request Line with details_ (`GET /transferRequestLines/{transferRequestLineId}`).

## Adding a new external account
This adding is needed when there is no registered external account that matches with the forcasted account identification (for instance `IBAN`). This new created external account may not be usable at once. Its activation may be delayed to be conform to security rules.

1. Add a new external account for the current customer in our systems with _Create a new external account_ (`POST /externalAccounts`).
1. In a general way, an error HTTP 403 is returned with a specific header "X-Stepup-Token" to indicate that is necessary for the caller application to enter into a step-up process (within a strong authentication) to seal the addition of the external account.
1. In presence of a such response, please call "BPCE_CONNECT" to enter into a step-up process.
1. After having do the strong authentification and completing the step-up process, redo a second call to _Create a new external account_ (`POST /externalAccounts`) with the access token that was just generated in order to do the create action.

## Canceling a transfer request

1. Cancel a transfer request with _Delete a transfer request_ (`DELETE /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}`). All the transfer request lines which are embedded by the transfer request are canceled.

## Canceling a transfer request line

1. Cancel a transfer request line with _Delete a transfer request line_ (`DELETE /transferRequests/{transferRequestId}/transferRequestLines/{transferRequestLineId}`). The other transfer request lines included in the same transfer request are not canceled.

delete.description: Delete a transfer request. All the transfer request lines which are embedded by the transfer request are canceled. Only delayed transfer lines with an execution date set in the future can be canceled.

post.description:
Confirm a transfer request. The entry phase is over with calling this endpoint. At first call of this endpoint, a strong authentication may be generally demanded in order to seal the transfer. So an HTTP error 403 is returned at first call with presence of a HTTP header called "X-Stepup-Token". In this case, the consumer must forward to "BPCE_CONNECT" urls to enter into a stepup process. After that, a second call of this endpoint will be possible and needed to really do the confirmation of the transfer request.
In particular and rare cases, besides the confirmation of the transfer request is necessary, it is not allowed at all via this API ; in this case, an HTTP 400 error with code "bpce.delegation.hasToBeDoneOnBankWebSite" indicates the end user customer to validate the transfer within the BPCE web site.

201.description: Confirmation of the transfer. The request goes into CONFIRMED status. It is no longer possible to modify the request (by adding lines for example).

ExecutionDeadlineType.title: ExecutionDeadlineType
ExecutionDeadlineType.description:
Execution delay type.
Code Meaning
INSTANT Within the minute (instant payment).
ASAP =As soon as possible (today). The transfer request lines may be processed in the following days.
DELAYED For a date in the future.

ExecutionFrequency.title: ExecutionFrequency
ExecutionFrequency.description:
Indicates if a transfer will be processed only one time or if it is a standing transfer.
Code Meaning
ONESHOT The transfer will be processed only one time
STANDING The transfer will be processed several times in a periodic way

ExecutionSettlement.title: Settlement
ExecutionSettlement.description:
Type of transfer processing chain used.
Code Meaning
INTERNAL Between two internal accounts belonging to the subscriber and managed by the same BPCE bank establishment.
SEPA SCT Transfer using the SEPA scheme.

ExecutionStatus.title: ExecutionStatus
ExecutionStatus.description:
Transfer processing status (i.e. a transfer request line status).
Status Meaning
TO_VALIDATE Needs to be validated.
VALIDATED Validated by the subscriber or by an authorized validator.
WAITING_DECISION Waiting for a decision.
PENDING Waiting for execution.
REFUSED Refused.
CANCELED Canceled by the subscriber.
REJECTED Rejected by the system.
EXECUTED Executed.
REFUNDED Refunded.
TERMINATED Terminated.
REJECTED_BY_RECIPIENT_BANK_AND_REFUNDED Transfer that has been rejected by the beneficiary bank and so the transfer request line is refunded in an individual way.

ExternalAccount.description: Characteristics of an account beneficiary for making transfers, authorized to the user of the subscription. This may be an IBAN registered by the subscriber to make transfers to third parties, but also a subset of his own accounts in the banking establishment and which are eligible for credit as part of a transfer account to account.

activationDateTime.description: If the beneficiary account is being activated, indicates the date from which it will be usable.

isHolder.description: Indicates whether the subscriber is the owner or co-owner of the beneficiary account. Declarative data.

groupLabels.description: Name of the beneficiary groups to which the account is attached.

ExternalAccountStatus.title: ExternalAccountStatus
ExternalAccountStatus.description:
Status of the external account (beneficiary).
Code Meaning
DELETED The external account has been canceled. It will not be usable anymore.
ACTIVATION_IN_PROGRESS The external account has been created but is not usable yet.
ACTIVATED The external account can be used for a new transfer.

EVERY_SIX_MONTHS Once every six months.
ANNUALLY Once every year.

RequestedTransferRequestDebitMode.title: RequestedTransferRequestDebitMode
RequestedTransferRequestDebitMode.description:
Indicates how the caller wishes the set of transfer request lines to be debited from the source account ; that is if there should be only one global accounting entry with the global amount or alternatively there should be n single transfers (one accounting entry for one transfer request line).
Code Meaning
GROUPED One global accounting entry with the global amount.
SINGLE One accounting entry for each transfer request line.

startDate.description: The start date for a standing transfer.

endDate.description: The last theoretical date for the standing transfer.

lastExecutionDate.description: The last actual date a transfer was actually made as part of this standing transfer order. It may be adjusted for calendar reasons.

TransferRequest.description: This resource stands for the wish from the caller to initiate a set of transfer. The size of the list of transfer request lines is valued to "1" for single transfer or be greater to initiate a multiple transfer.

TransferRequestDebitMode.title: TransferRequestDebitMode
TransferRequestDebitMode.description:
Indicates how the set of transfer request lines are debited from the source account ; that is if there is only one global accounting entry with the global amount or alternatively there are n single transfers (one accounting entry for one transfer request line).
Code Meaning
GROUPED One global accounting entry with the global amount.
SINGLE One accounting entry for each transfer request line.

TransferRequestStatus.title: TransferRequestStatus
TransferRequestStatus.description:
State of the transfer request. This state is useful to follow and manage a transfer request only during the entry phase. Once confirmed, rejected or canceled, the transfer request is in a terminal state and will not change, so that it is the state of the transfer request line one must then examinate to know if a transfer have been well processed or not.
Code Meaning
INITIALIZED The transfer request has been accepted but all transfer lines has not been processed so that the transfer request confirmation step is not yet available.
CONFIRMABLE The transfer request has been accepted and all transfer lines has been processed so that the transfer request confirmation step is available.
CONFIRMED The transfer request has been confirmed. One cannot add additional transfer lines to the transfer request anymore.
REJECTED The BPCE system has rejected all the lines (for a common cause).
DELETED The subscriber has canceled the transfer request (all lines are canceled).

TransferRequestSummary.description: Summary of a transfer request. This resource includes only global information of the request. There is no information about the lines details here. The globalAmount property is a free of charge amount.

transferRequestId.description: Identifier related to the transfer request

globalAmount.description: Global amount of the transfer request.

transfersCount.description: Number of transfers included in this request.

creationDateTime.description: Date and time of creation for the request.

modificationDateTime.description: Date and time of modification for the request.

globalFee.description: Global fees of the transfer request.
